journeys.title: A useful paid model request
journeys.subtitle: Existing extraction source and the hosted-run target share account and money gates. Full paid acceptance remains open.
steps: Use current authenticated identity and a qualified model offer.
A verified payment fulfills once; entitlement or a balance alone does not admit a run.
AccountLedger owns the hold, fee/caps and settlement identity.
Hosted target: persist run, attempt, fence and unresolved supplier liability before scheduling.
Hosted target: one Temporal workflow drives retries, cancellation and worker-loss recovery.
Existing extraction source calls Grip/Modal. Hosted target uses a qualified worker/provider.
Unknown effects stay unresolved. Publish the exact usable result and durable history only with current scope.
notes: The observed web/API health has no serving revision and does not pass the paid journey.
Existing Grip extraction is a source-wired direct path. PostgreSQL + Mesh + Temporal is the hosted target, not proof of deployed current wiring.
Lost responses reconcile the same operation identity. A retry cannot double-charge or release unresolved supplier exposure.

journeys.title: QQ develops and updates itself
journeys.subtitle: The real cycle must produce a useful QQ-authored fix, independent evidence, a PR and recoverable adoption.
steps: Retain the current failure, session identity and expected behavior.
Check exact runtime, credentials, workspace and preserved state. Provider readiness is still open.
One author changes a bounded candidate in an isolated worktree. Preserve concurrent edits.
Compare baseline and candidate on the real normal, failure and recovery paths.
A non-author evaluates current source and actual behavior. New pushes stale the verdict.
Publish the reviewable candidate and report hosted CI separately.
Select a qualified version, preserve the same session, then verify follow-up and rollback.
notes: The dated installed-runtime trial had zero model starts. No complete QQ-authored self-development cycle is accepted.
The required order is detect errors, assess the environment, repair, verify, and create a pull request. Independent review and qualified adoption complete the cycle.
A source fix, successful compilation, helper fixture, PR or update receipt cannot replace a useful provider response and preserved-session recovery.
